newsitem.title: USA: Packard Bell settles with states over computer parts.
newsitem.headline: Packard Bell settles with states over computer parts.

text.p: Packard Bell will pay more than $1.5 million as part of a multi-state agreement to settle allegations it sold computers as "new" when they contained parts from computers returned by customers, Pennsylvania Attorney General Tom Corbett said Thursday.
Without admitting wrongdoing, the privately held computer company agreed to pay $70,000 in legal fees and investigative costs to each of the 22 states involved in the settlement, Corbett said.
However, the Sacramento, Calif.-based company will continue recycling components from returned personal computers, which it says is a common practice among major personal computer manufacturers.

But Packard Bell agreed to place a prominent notice explaining the practice on the cartons of all computers and monitors it sells as "new" but which may contain components from previously sold computers.
The company also must provide retailers with point of display materials to inform consumers of the practice.
It will begin the notification programme in January.
"In addition, such components must be covered by the Packard Bell original product warranty for new products," Corbett said.
Packard Bell contends that the quality of properly disassembled and retested components from returned computers are functionally equivalent or superior to "new" components.

In addition to Pennsylvania, the other states involved in the agreement are Arizona, Arkansas, California, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Texas, West Virginia and Vermont.
